Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD)

In 12 patients, one PBM session increased six-minute walk distance but did not change spirometry, respiratory pressures, or thoracoabdominal mobility. A second crossover study reported more steps in six minutes after combined light and magnetic-field treatment. Long-term respiratory benefit is not established.

PBM Database summary

What the records report

In 12 patients, one PBM session increased six-minute walk distance but did not change spirometry, respiratory pressures, or thoracoabdominal mobility. A second crossover study reported more steps in six minutes after combined light and magnetic-field treatment. Long-term respiratory benefit is not established.

Summary of the Evidence

The exact Respiratory system > COPD category contains 13 titles: eight human reports, three mouse experiments, one narrative review, and one trial protocol. The human records include five randomized trials and three other clinical reports. The protocol and review are not new participant cohorts. Overlap among reports from recurring research groups is not fully resolved.

Human and clinical evidence

The most clearly reported sham-controlled crossover trial randomized 12 men with COPD to active or sham PBM at the main respiratory muscles. Six-minute walk distance increased after active treatment, while spirometry, maximal respiratory pressures, and thoracoabdominal mobility did not show significant between-condition interactions (de Souza et al. 2020). A 21-person crossover study combining laser diodes, LEDs, and a magnetic field reported improved six-minute step-test performance (Miranda et al. 2019). Other small clinical reports examine exercise performance, dyspnea, or respiratory measures, but use different designs and treatment combinations. The narrative review synthesizes these same reports rather than adding patients (Lu et al. 2023).

Animal evidence

Three mouse experiments model smoke-related COPD or pulmonary inflammation. They report immune or inflammatory changes, not patient-level breathing, exercise, or exacerbation outcomes (de Brito et al. 2024).

In-vitro and ex-vivo evidence

No standalone in-vitro or ex-vivo study is listed in the exact COPD category. A separate asthma-COPD-overlap cell model is adjacent evidence and should not be counted as a COPD patient study.

Treatment Parameters and Generalizability

One crossover trial used a cluster of red 630-nm and near-infrared 830-nm LEDs on respiratory muscles. Wavelength is the light's color band and affects tissue penetration. Other reports apply light to working muscles or combine it with a magnetic field, so protocols cannot be assumed equivalent.

Interpretation

The observed gains are acute exercise-test results from small studies. The null spirometry and pressure findings matter for respiratory claims. Replicated trials with larger samples, patient-centered symptoms, and longer follow-up are needed before inferring durable COPD benefit.

Evidence strength in source summaryLow for acute gains in walking or step-test performance in small randomized COPD studies Very low for changes in spirometry, durable respiratory function, or reduced exacerbations
Publications and records13 titles (exact Respiratory system > COPD)

Evidence strength rationale and next steps

Small randomized crossover studies report immediate improvements in walking or stepping performance, while the respiratory measurements tested in one trial were unchanged. Other reports use different interventions and designs. Larger sham-controlled studies should assess clinically meaningful daily activity, breathing symptoms, and persistence rather than only same-day exercise tests.
